name: Libertarian Socialism
summary: Libertarian socialism is an anti-authoritarian, anti-capitalist current that seeks workers' self-management and direct democracy, rejecting both private ownership of the means of production and state ownership. It spans anarchist currents and libertarian Marxist ones such as council communism, and favours federated, decentralised organisation from below with direct action as its method.
scope: The mainstream of the family: the social-anarchist and council-communist core (Proudhon, Bakunin, Kropotkin, Pannekoek, Luxemburg) as presented by Daniel Guerin and Noam Chomsky. Where strands differ, answers follow that shared anti-state, anti-capitalist core; individualist and market-socialist strands, and democratic-socialist currents in the British labour movement, are noted but not followed. Many answers not stated in these sources are carried over from the anarchist profile and marked low.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Social libertarian socialists reject capitalist markets as a source of exploitation, though they oppose state allocation too and the mutualist minority keeps markets among co-operatives.

public-ownership.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject state ownership as bureaucratic control; Pannekoek called it state capitalism and Chomsky cites Bakunin's warning of a red bureaucracy.

unions-good.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists built unions as schools of self-management, but council communists such as Pannekoek rejected trade unions as bureaucratic, so the strands split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Capitalist property relations are called incompatible with freedom, though personal self-ownership is upheld.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale turns on whether regulation should be tighter than now, or on replacing corporations instead of regulating them, and the statement now asks whether corporations should face strict government regulation.

reviewHistory.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose corporations as hierarchical institutions and want them replaced by self-management; they would curb corporate power, but distrust state regulation as the remedy.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers' control of production is the core economic demand, whether through cooperatives or common ownership.

strong-leader.rationale: Rejection of rulers and of any concentrated authority over others is the definition of anarchism.

state-harmful.rationale: The tradition is anti-statist, but Chomsky and democratic-socialist strands see government as accountable and sometimes a needed defence against private power, so not all call it simply harmful.

decide-locally.rationale: Federalism and decentralised self-governance are central, as the article and Chomsky describe.

rehabilitation.rationale: Libertarian socialists see crime as largely produced by property and privilege and want prisons abolished; between the two options they reject punishment, though they also reject the prison itself.

more-religion-public.rationale: Most libertarian socialists are atheists who see religion as a justification of earthly authority, following Bakunin's rejection of God as master; Christian anarchism is a minority strand.

gradual-change.rationale: Most favour revolutionary or prefigurative change, though some pursue reforms while keeping anti-capitalist aims.

free-trade.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose capitalist globalization, prominently in the anti-WTO protests, as serving capital rather than workers, while also opposing national protectionism.

open-borders.rationale: Anarchist and internationalist strands reject nation-state borders, but the article does not state it as core.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Libertarian socialists hold that social problems stem from hierarchy and property, which technology alone cannot fix; social ecology accepts appropriate technology while primitivists reject it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Social revolution is the stated aim of most, but reformist and nonviolent strands exist and the article records the reformism debate.

central-planning.rationale: They favour decentralised, council-based coordination from below rather than a central authority, which Pannekoek treats as a new ruling class.

socialized-markets.rationale: Mutualists and market socialists accept worker-owned markets, while communist strands reject markets altogether.

basic-income.rationale: An unconditional income from the state conflicts with anti-statism and with communists' aim to abolish money, but some contemporary libertarian socialists support it as relief; adherents are split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject state control of the economy, holding production should be directed by federated producers' associations.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Mutualists and individualists favour small producers' possession of their means of work, while the social anarchist majority prefers collective possession and warns that individual ownership can recreate bosses and landlords.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The wage system is rejected as exploitative; Pannekoek proposes labour-time accounting in place of wages, while money abolition is held mainly by communist strands.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Libertarian socialists would abolish central banks with the state, but most reject leaving money to the market, aiming instead at mutual banks or the end of money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies uniting employers and workers contradict both anarchist anti-statism and the abolition of the employer class.

one-party-rule.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject any party ruling the state, which they see as government by a new privileged minority.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Anarchism rejects all forms of rule, from monarchies to republics.

democracy-best.rationale: They endorse direct and council democracy but reject parliamentary representation, so the statement as worded splits them.

direct-votes.rationale: Direct democracy is described as central, though councils work through mandated delegates rather than mass votes on all laws.

workers-councils.rationale: Council communism and anarcho-syndicalism put power in councils elected directly by workers, as Pannekoek and Chomsky describe.

natural-rulers.rationale: Libertarian socialists hold that no one should dominate another; human differences must never be turned into power.

political-violence-never.rationale: Strands disagree: pacifists reject it, while Goldman and Malatesta saw it as sometimes a necessary evil.

separate-church-state.rationale: Libertarian socialists want neither state nor church authority and are strongly anti-clerical where churches hold power, so they reject any union of the two.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject laws as such and religion as a basis of authority; even Christian libertarian socialists reject state law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Social libertarian socialists reject capitalist firms as hierarchical and want defence and dispute resolution handled by free associations and arbitration; Tucker's individualist minority accepted private defence associations.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Direct action and class conflict are named as the means of social revolution, though not all adopt the historical-materialist claim.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Libertarian socialists seek social equality and communists distribute by need, which goes beyond equal opportunity, though they reject identical treatment of unequal individuals.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Social libertarian socialists see solidarity as enlightened self-interest and the egoist strand embraces self-interest outright, while rejecting capitalist individualism; adherents are split on framing it as a moral good.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Green libertarian socialists and deep ecologists affirm nature's intrinsic value, while social ecology, the most influential current, rejects deep ecology as anti-human; split.

restore-past-order.rationale: Libertarian socialists seek a new, stateless and classless society, not the restoration of past hierarchies.

direct-action.rationale: Direct action over electoral politics is named as the route to social revolution.

means-match-ends.rationale: Libertarian socialists hold that the means of change should embody the free society sought, as Chomsky's emphasis on self-organisation and SEP's account of anarchist means say.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Primitivists reject civilization, but mainstream social libertarian socialists such as Kropotkin envisage a decentralised, technologically advanced society and most reject primitivism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Kropotkin's 'all for all' favours need, though Pannekoek's early stage ties consumption to work.

production-for-use.rationale: They aim to replace profit-driven production with democratic planning from below to meet needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Capitalism is held to rest on labour exploitation, and wage labour conflicts with producer control.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rejected as state power that produces a red bureaucracy, per Chomsky citing Bakunin and Pannekoek's critique of party rule.

collective-farming.rationale: Social libertarian socialists want land held in common and worked by free associations, as in the Spanish collectives, but reject forced collectivisation and allow individual farmers who work the land themselves.

harm-principle.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject laws that govern consenting adults' private conduct, but they deny the state any power at all, including the harm-prevention role the statement grants it.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individualist libertarian socialists put the individual's rights against all groups, while social libertarian socialists stress communal good and some support collective national liberation; libertarian socialists are split.

state-as-business.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose both the state and capitalist ownership, so a state owned and run like a company is doubly rejected.

positive-liberty.rationale: Social libertarian socialists hold that real freedom requires equality and the means to live, which is why they seek common ownership and distribution by need.

organic-representation.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject parties and would organise society through federations of communes and workers' associations, though they want mandated delegates rather than corporatist representation.

total-state.rationale: Anarchism seeks to abolish the state altogether.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Libertarian socialists are anti-imperialist and anti-militarist and reject state borders altogether.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose all hierarchical authority, including personal lordship.

bound-labor.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose all forced labour and want land free to those who work it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers' self-management without bosses, appointed by employers or the state, is the defining demand.

economic-freedom.rationale: Libertarian socialists see capitalist property and wage labour as forms of domination that undermine freedom, so for them political freedom requires ending, not protecting, market economic 'freedom'.

rule-by-example.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject rule itself and hold that authority corrupts rulers as well as the ruled, so they would not rely on rulers' example; they also reject laws and punishments, so the rejection of the statement is partial.

class-collaboration.rationale: Libertarian socialists call wage labor wage slavery and seek to abolish the wage system and capitalism rather than make peace with employers.

dominated-front.rationale: Libertarian socialists support anti-colonial struggle but distrust state and nationalist fronts, so they are split.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose patriarchy and have an anarcha-feminist strand, and they reject law imposing roles on anyone.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose hierarchy and the state's power to classify and coerce, and stand in solidarity with migrants against nationalism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Kropotkin saw the state as an instrument of landlordism and capitalism; Chomsky stresses wealthy-class control while allowing it can be held accountable.

proportional-representation.rationale: Malatesta and the social anarchist tradition reject parliament and voting as a route to freedom, so tinkering with seat allocation is not their goal.

national-mission.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose the state and nationalism and are internationalist and anti-militarist, so exporting a national government is rejected.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Anarchism extends its critique of hierarchy to patriarchy, and anarcha-feminism is an established strand.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Libertarian socialists hold that government is a class instrument that corrupts those who rule and serves privilege against ordinary people.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Libertarian socialists seek to abolish the state altogether and see police and army as tools of exploitation and property.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Anarchism rejects hierarchy and treats all people as equals, but it rejects state law, so 'rights before the law' is only partly its framing.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Libertarian socialists defend free thought and oppose state coercion in matters of belief.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Bakunin's critique of Marxism held that a strong transitional state entrenches a new ruling class; libertarian socialists want the state abolished at once.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Libertarian socialists hold that only voluntary association is legitimate, though they reject the very idea of being governed.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of minorities contradicts the anti-authoritarian and internationalist principles.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Pacifist strands accept it, but expropriation and sabotage are defended by others, and property is defined differently.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Libertarian socialists share the anarchist and council-communist view that cooperation and solidarity, not competition, are the basis of a good society.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Libertarian socialists hold that wage labour and hierarchical authority make people unfree even when the boss does not interfere, which is why they call for self-management.

vanguard-party.rationale: Libertarian socialism rejects vanguard parties, and council communists such as Pannekoek held that workers' councils must run their own struggle.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Direct action and workers organising from below are core, and they distrust state limits on it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: They are anti-authoritarian and oppose emergency state powers.

party-controls-media.rationale: They reject state control and favour free, decentralised organisation from below, which excludes state or party control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: Pannekoek and the anarchists reject state and party power, and favour workers militias over a party army.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Rejecting the state means rejecting a ruler commanding armed forces and choosing ministers; the family prefers armed people and no standing executive.

clerical-rule.rationale: Anarchists and council communists reject rule by clergy as authority that is both statist and religious.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Anti-war internationalists in this family, from Bakunin to Luxemburg, treat inter-imperialist war as a ruling-class affair and urge opposition to one own government; adherents split on tactics.

recall-officials.rationale: Revocable, mandated delegates are a central principle of council democracy and direct democracy.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Nothing in the tradition ranks countryside above city morally; Kropotkin wanted to integrate town and country, so this is an inference at low confidence.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The tradition values workers' own knowledge, but its attitude to intellectuals is mixed (Chomsky criticises technocrats, others rely on intellectuals); no clear position.

religious-exemptions.rationale: They oppose coercion by the state but also religious authority, so exemptions for believers are not a settled position.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Council communists and anarchists distrust parliamentary bodies and favour councils and federations, yet some accept an elected assembly as a transitional step; adherents are split.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject authoritarian state development as the opposite of self-management and freedom.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject private ownership of the means of production in favour of common control, though they go further than limiting use.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Pannekoek and other council communists explicitly described Soviet Russia as state capitalism, and anarchists likewise denied it was socialist.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: They are strongly anti-clerical but oppose strengthening state power over anyone; most would abolish clerical privilege through social action, not state control.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on general self-government, separate laws or no stated position, not on keeping a distinct economic system, and the statement now asks only whether a region joining a larger state should be free to keep its economic system.

reviewHistory.rationale: Federalist, decentralised self-government with communities arranging their own affairs is core to the tradition, though they want no state above the region either.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

sacred-ruler.rationale: The tradition rejects both hierarchical authority and religious dogma, so a sacred ruler is the opposite of its anti-authoritarian core.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Adherents reject rulers and rule by decree altogether, so a sovereign above the law is opposed.

space-expansion.rationale: The tradition has no position on space; some embrace post-scarcity technology while others stress local ecological limits, so adherents are split.

mixed-constitution.rationale: They reject rule by a ruling few and want power exercised by all through direct democracy and councils, not a blend with aristocratic elements.

leader-cult.rationale: Glorifying leaders contradicts the tradition's anti-authoritarian, self-managing principles.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Council communists warned that party rule leads to state capitalism, so they accept that leaders can restore capitalism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Anarchists reject coercion over belief and state enforcement of religion.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Direct democracy is favoured, but anarchists also reject majority coercion and state courts; split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Council communists rejected vanguard leadership and want working-class self-emancipation; anarchist views on armed action are mixed.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Abolition of hierarchy and privilege is central to anarchism.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject domination of one people by another, and Chomsky's anti-imperialism makes this a clear rejection.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose the state, nationalism and imperial power, so cultivating imperial-style influence is rejected.

minority-veto.rationale: Consensus and the right of exit appeal to many, yet councils and assemblies decide by majority; strands differ.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Self-management and direct democracy require ordinary people to take part in public affairs.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Rejects both but many in the family refuse to equate them, as Chomsky does; adherents split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Anti-authoritarian and opposed to standing armies; a political guardian role is the opposite of the tradition.

office-by-exam.rationale: They want officials chosen and recalled by communities and councils, not an appointed bureaucratic class selected by examination.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Council communism and direct democracy make delegates instructed by and recallable at any time by those who chose them.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Social anarchists hold land in common, with individuals having possession only while using it, in contrast to private property.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Imperial intervention to enforce a bloc is state domination and runs against self-determination and federalism.

corporate-influence.rationale: Chomsky and the anti-capitalist tradition hold that concentrated private power captures the state.

job-guarantee.rationale: Adherents are split between wanting work guaranteed through self-managed enterprises and objecting to the state as employer.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Anarchist currents deny that the state's authority creates a general duty to obey, which the Stanford entry treats as core.

industrial-unions.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists favoured industrial unionism, but Pannekoek and council communists preferred workplace councils over unions, so the strands split.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Chomsky stresses transparency against concentrated power; not a central doctrine.

local-production.rationale: Kropotkin's decentralised economy of integrated local production supports this, though federations trade over distance.

religious-nation.rationale: Adherents are internationalists who reject religious authority as a basis for political community.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Libertarian socialists want common control of productive property, not of personal belongings.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Self-governing communes and federated councils owning property in common are central to the family.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The family rejects both private ownership and state ownership of production.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Rejecting state coercion over personal life and the criminal law as an instrument of authority, adherents oppose criminalising consensual relations.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Suppressing opposition is the practice of the state and dictatorship that the ideology rejects, and it criticised the Bolsheviks for exactly this.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Adherents are anti-clerical and oppose any state enforcing religion; punishing blasphemy would be authority at its worst.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anti-imperialism and internationalism follow from rejecting exploitation and the state; colonial rule for the ruler's benefit is exploitation.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct self-management by those affected, in workplaces and communities through federated assemblies, is the core of the ideology's alternative to the state.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The family is anti-capitalist and on the left, though it rejects the authoritarian left and some adherents say old labels mislead.

alienated-labor.rationale: Chomsky's discussion of Humboldt and Marx treats wage labour as alienating, and workers' self-management as its remedy.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Atheism and the rejection of all authority are central, as in Bakunin's anarchist critique of God and the state.

social-market-economy.rationale: Both markets and wage relations are rejected, and the state-regulated compromise is rejected as well; production and distribution are to be organised in common.

rich-first.rationale: Equality and abolition of class privilege are central; letting some get rich first contradicts them.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject hierarchical authority and hereditary power, which contradict their commitment to self-management.

property-franchise.rationale: Libertarian socialists favour direct democracy and equal participation and reject class-based limits on political rights.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Bookchin's social ecology and anarcha-feminism, both within the libertarian-socialist family, tie ending hierarchy among people to the domination of nature.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Chomsky's work argues that concentrated wealth shapes the press and limits real freedom, a view widely shared in the tradition.

racial-franchise.rationale: The tradition stands for equal participation and opposes domination by any group, so it rejects racial limits on political rights.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Libertarian socialists hold that no authority should control private life, so they reject legal marriage limits.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Chomsky's account of anarchism opposes concentrated private power over workers as incompatible with freedom, and the family aims at workers' self-management.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Chomsky's account of wage slavery and workers' control holds that income should come from useful work, not ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The SEP notes that most anarchists accept defensive violence even while rejecting aggressive force, so total pacifism is a minority view.

independent-unions.rationale: Libertarian socialists want workers to organise and control their own unions and councils, free of state or party direction.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Chomsky and the council communists call state ownership without workers' control state capitalism, not socialism.

municipal-property.rationale: Libertarian socialism favours social ownership by workers and communities rather than private owners or the state, though strands differ on whether the owner is the workplace or the community.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Council and anarchist federalism has delegates who coordinate while decisions stay with local assemblies and councils.

person-over-state.rationale: The anarchist core of the strand puts individual freedom above the state, and Chomsky traces it to Enlightenment liberalism.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject the state's monopoly of force and favour armed popular militias, as in Guerin's account of the Spanish revolution.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Chomsky and Guerin describe the core view that the state must be dismantled and replaced by federated workers' councils from below.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Federated, decentralised communities choosing their own arrangements fit the anti-blueprint strand, though most still expect collective ownership.

sacred-nation.rationale: Libertarian socialists are internationalist and anti-nationalist, rejecting the nation as a source of authority.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Chomsky argues for an innate human nature that grounds a drive for freedom and cooperation, and Kropotkin grounds mutual aid in it, though others stress its malleability.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The council tradition sees democracy as direct self-management by workers and communities, not merely competitive elections of rulers.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The profile rejects private ownership of the means of production, and the individualist strand that accepts it is excluded.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Council communists such as Pannekoek denounced the Soviet state as state capitalism, and the tradition rejects bureaucratic rule.

indirect-election.rationale: Pannekoek's workers' councils send recallable delegates upward from local councils, and federated delegation is a standard anarchist form.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Its anti-authoritarian, anti-state core rejects state killing without trial, as it opposes the state's coercive apparatus generally.

self-ownership.rationale: Social anarchists value individual freedom but reject self-ownership as the basis for private property in labour's product; strands differ.

no-business-privileges.rationale: It opposes state-capitalist alliances and holds that state power serves privileged owners, so it rejects special privileges for business.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Chomsky and the social-anarchist core hold that wage labour and concentrated property are unjust whatever the exchanges, so outcomes and power matter.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Strands differ: the anti-state core distrusts state taxes, while Chomsky-style writers have favoured limits on speculation; the sources do not settle it.

material-over-identity.rationale: Strands differ: council communists stress class, while many libertarian socialists today treat identity and class as linked.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Chomsky rejects state ownership and party rule as new masters, and the family insists on workers' own control of the economy.

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose the state, nationalism and imperial power, so cultivating imperial-style influence is rejected. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

notes: The family is broad: individualist and market-socialist strands accept markets, democratic-socialist strands accept the state, and pacifist strands reject violence. Answers not stated in the four sources were carried over from the anarchist profile and are marked low; another audit is not a source.
